$comment: The 0b canary ledger (TDD docs/tdd-ground-truth-remediation.md §4.2).
A P0 shipped in which api_route_forbids_sensitive_response_fields was structurally
incapable of firing while looking covered: both halves of the seam had tests, and both
tests hand-built the accepted contract. This file makes 'can this cell actually fire?' a
declared, checked property instead of an assumption.
THE UNIT IS THE PAIR (kind x enforcement path), NOT THE KIND. check_command.rs dispatches
on `is_presence_convention` - matcher.enforcement_semantics == 'presence' - BEFORE it
reaches any kind arm, and presence is stamped per CANDIDATE, not per kind
(candidate_command.rs:1240). So one kind can reach two different enforcement paths
depending on which candidate the proposer emitted, and a ledger keyed on kind alone would
declare a cell covered on the strength of a test that never entered it.
STATE MAY ONLY BE WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS:
firing        - a passing canary driving the documented workflow: >=1 finding on a
violation fixture, 0 on a conformance fixture.
quarantined   - a citation (doc path or code comment) stating the quarantine, quoted in
`citation`, PLUS a test asserting no findings.
unimplemented - a passing test proving the proposer emits no candidate of this shape.
needs-review  - the DEFAULT, assigned whenever the other three could not be produced.
needs-review IS NOT A FAILURE. Assigning `quarantined` by inference is - it is a claim
about intent, and guessing it converts an undiscovered P0 into a checked-in 'working as
designed', which is exactly how D1 survived. Every needs-review row names the evidence it
lacked in `missing_evidence`; that list is the next audit's worklist.
WHO EDITS THIS. Track C owns the structure and the enumeration, and the initial states its
own evidence supports. State TRANSITIONS are made by the lead at integration time (§4.2),
never speculatively on the strength of another track's in-flight work.
CI enforcement (scripts/convention-cell-ledger.mjs) activates on the INTEGRATION BRANCH
ONLY. Enforcing it on track branches would break the zero-file-overlap property: Track A's
D1 work earns the sensitive-fields transition, but this is Track C's file on a branch
forked before C merged.

enforcement.note: On any other branch the checker reports and exits 0. See §4.2 'Scope of that CI rule'.
enforcement.needs_review_note: `needs-review` is a PASSING state by default. docs/decisions/ledger-needs-review.md proposes tightening it, and ships the mechanism: with DRIFT_LEDGER_STRICT_NEEDS_REVIEW=1 on an enforcing branch, a needs-review cell whose `receipt_evidence.reached` is not true becomes a failure. Default OFF because all six of today's needs-review cells would fail it, and the flip is a human call about whether an unmeasured kind may ship - not a change to make as a side effect of building the measurement.

citation.symbol: The decision - option (b), fail closed at acceptance
citation.quote: The arm was unreachable three times over: both proposers stamp `enforcement_capability: "heuristic_check"` where the engine loop requires `deterministic_check`; packages/cli/src/check/run-check.ts contains zero occurrences of the kind, so the engine is never invoked for it; and graph_service_delegation_findings took `_allowed_delegate_imports` and never read it, so the matcher's only configurable field had no effect.
citation.second_quote: Refuse rather than store a rule nothing evaluates: an accepted convention with no evaluator produces no finding on any repo and reports a clean pass, which reads as "checked, and fine".

cells.missing_evidence: Corrected 2026-08-16 on branch glob-revival/safeparse. The old text said no fixture can produce ANY candidate of this kind; that is now false - test/fixtures/gt-request-validation produces the per-symbol candidate, and the sibling request_validation_proof cell is `firing` on it. The presence half remains blocked, and for a reason that no fixture can lift: FAMILY_SPECS (candidate_command.rs:891-908) sources the request-validation family from the `request_validation_called` fact kind ONLY - `symbol_called` is deliberately excluded, because including it produced an 89-member family on dub. But `request_validation_called` facts are produced by extract_security_facts only when accepted validators are already passed in, and the scan path calls the 3-arg `extract_security_facts` (main.rs:663), whose wrapper hard-codes the empty validator slice when it delegates (security_facts.rs:20) - the `&[]` at the call site is `accepted_auth_helpers`, not the validators. So at scan time - the only time the proposer reads facts - zero `request_validation_called` facts exist in any repo, and the family can never form. This is a code gap, not a corpus gap: no fixture can supply a fact kind the scanner never emits. Fixing main.rs:663 to feed the accepted validators into the scan was explicitly out of scope for the glob-revival sprint.

cells.canary: test/e2e/gt-canary.test.ts :: phase-5 secret-exposure path fires, reached by contract import
cells.evidence: Re-derived. The old row's first claim still holds and is still pinned: candidate_command.rs contains zero occurrences of this kind, so the proposer emits nothing of this shape, and both `proposer emits no candidate of the unimplemented shapes` (security-secret-leak) and an assertNoProposerFor check inside the new canary's own run continue to assert it. Its second claim - `nothing can ever reach it` - was false. `drift contract import drift.lock --repo <id> --confirm` (docs/agent-integration.md:84, router.ts:158, contract.ts:452) is a documented path for a kind with no proposer, and through it the arm fires end to end: on gt-secret-exposure, with the proposer's own literal scope ["**/app/api/**/route.ts", "**/app/api/**/route.tsx", "**/pages/api/**/*.ts"] (candidate_command.rs:372) so phase5_file_scope_matches -> path_glob_matches is genuinely exercised, `check --scope changed-hunks` emits exactly 2 block-mode findings - app/api/billing/route.ts:3 (secret to Response.json) and app/api/webhooks/route.ts:3 (secret to console.error) - names app/api/status/route.ts as a conforming example, and exits 2. Verified by mutation: stubbing path_glob_matches back to the pre-fix behaviour turns both findings into zero and the canary red. So this cell is `firing` with no proposer path, which is a state the ledger's vocabulary allows and the old row conflated.

cells.canary: test/e2e/gt-canary.test.ts > phase-4 tenant-scope path fires, and the helper-scoped siblings pass
cells.evidence: gt-tenant-scope: the proposer emits exactly one candidate of this kind (required_calls [requireTenantScope]; scope.path_globs the literal proposer set, **/app/api/**/route.ts included), accepted through `conventions accept --severity error --mode block`. 3 findings — app/api/projects/route.ts:4 with actual_layer tenant_predicate_missing and enforcement_result block, plus the two §4.3 near-miss routes that call throwIfTenantScopeMismatch. 0 findings on the two routes that call the accepted helper, and those two carry phase-4 proofs with tenant.required=true and tenant.proven=true, so they were evaluated and passed rather than skipped. Exit 2 over a diff of all five routes; exit 0 over a diff of the two scoped routes. Required one engine fix: security_proof.rs's untrusted-tenant-source clause counted a scoped_helper predicate as a route-supplied tenant value, which made this kind able to report a violation but never a pass.

Accepted in block mode it yields 3 findings - projects/route.ts:7 and reports/route.ts:14 authorization_guard_missing, audits/route.ts:10 authorization_guard_not_dominating_sink - check exits 2, and 0 findings on members/ and invoices/, each of which carries an authorization proof with required=true, proven=true in the same run.

cells.canary: test/e2e/gt-canary.test.ts > phase-4 session-trust path fires through contract import
cells.evidence: Two claims, and they are not one claim. (1) THE PROPOSER STILL EMITS NOTHING OF THIS SHAPE. candidate_command.rs contains zero occurrences of ConventionKind::SessionObjectMustComeFromTrustedHelper, and both fixtures built for it (security-session-trusted-helper, security-session-from-request-untrusted) still yield an empty candidate list; 'proposer emits no candidate of the unimplemented shapes' continues to assert exactly that, unweakened. (2) THE ENFORCEMENT ARM IS NEVERTHELESS REACHABLE, AND FIRES. The previous evidence inferred from (1) that the arm 'is unreachable through the documented workflow'; that inference was wrong, because 'drift contract import drift.lock --repo <id> --confirm' IS a documented workflow (docs/agent-integration.md:84, router.ts:158, contract.ts:199). Driven end to end over test/fixtures/gt-session-trust with a contract carrying the proposer's own literal scope globs, the phase-4 arm (check_command.rs:1636,1645) emits one finding at app/api/session/route.ts:4, title 'API route uses untrusted session object', severity error, enforcement_result block, exit code 2 at --scope changed-hunks. The compliant sibling app/api/profile/route.ts is silent AND carries session_trust {required: true, proven: true}, so it was evaluated rather than skipped. The glob scope filter at check_command.rs:1610-1618 is on that path: with path_glob_matches reverted to the pre-fix prefix behaviour the canary fails with zero findings.

citation.quote: Kinds `ConventionKindSchema` accepts that no evaluator implements. Established by searching both evaluators for every declared kind: the engine-owned `crates/drift-engine/src/check_command.rs` and the CLI-owned `packages/cli/src/check/run-check.ts`. These three appear in neither, so a contract declaring one produces no finding on any repo, ever, and nothing reports that - `check` returns a clean pass. "Accepted and silently enforcing nothing" is the one thing Drift must not let a user believe, so acceptance refuses them instead of storing an inert rule.
citation.second_quote: Refuse rather than store a rule nothing evaluates: an accepted convention with no evaluator produces no finding on any repo and reports a clean pass, which reads as "checked, and fine".

cells.note: This is the state's evidence bar met literally: a located code comment declaring the non-enforcement deliberate, plus a test asserting zero findings. It is recorded as `quarantined` rather than `unimplemented` because this ledger's `unimplemented` means the PROPOSER emits nothing, and here it does. The citation's own words are 'until one is implemented', so a reviewer disputing the label has the text to dispute it with.
